questions: How many bars did you measure on the 2.0 nm wafer, over how many cooldowns, and how many showed the field-free diode and the [100] reversal?
Why were the others set aside?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: preparation fields beyond ±1 T along [100] (Fig. 3d), measurement fields near zero, and temperatures above 20 mK?
What does the second-best device look like, for example the [100] bar's zero-field-cooled switching distributions and the Fig. 3b readout?

Does a prepared polarity survive warming the bar above TC at H = 0 and cooling back, and why do the switching currents after preparation (Fig. 3b axis, about 16 to 23 µA) sit below those after zero-field cooling (Fig. 3a inset, about 27 to 31 µA)?
How did you set and check H = 0 after the ±1 T and ±4 T excursions, and did [100] and [010] fields come from different magnet coils for both bars?

What local field at the Al does the SQUID bound allow? By my estimate, 3×10−3 µB/Mn is about 0.6 emu/cm3 (4πM near 8 G), so fields of order a gauss near edges or domain walls seem possible, the scale at which Hou et al. see diodes in plain films.
Why does the Fig. 4 reference come from a different wafer ("a CuMnAs wafer with 3 nm fully oxidized Al cap", p. 8) measured at 5 K, and could Reven or XMLD-PEEM be measured on the diode wafer itself?
